lessons.title: Question: Built-in Middleware
lessons.interactiveContent:
What are built-in middleware functions?

Functions that Express provides to perform actions between request and responseFunctions that you create to perform actions between request and responseFunctions that other parties create for you to use

Functions that Express provides to perform actions between request and response.
lessons.hardModeContent:
An app uses express.json() to prepare a request body before a route handler runs. What kind of middleware is this?

Built-in middleware provided by ExpressCustom middleware created by the app developerThird-party middleware installed as another packageResponse middleware that runs only after res.send()

Built-in middleware provided by Express.

lessons.title: Question: router.param()
lessons.interactiveContent:
What kind of route does the router.param(name, callback) method match?

Any route that uses the :name parameter and matches the current requestAny route that matches the current request

Any route that uses the :name parameter and matches the current request.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A router defines /users/:name, /teams/:name, and /about. Which requests can trigger router.param("name", callback)?

Matching requests to both routes that contain :nameEvery matching request, including /aboutOnly a request whose path is exactly /name

Matching requests to both routes that contain :name.

lessons.title: Question: Built-in Middleware
lessons.interactiveContent:
Why are built-in middleware functions useful?

To help the server parse bodies, encode URLs, and so onTo help the server respondThey are not useful; we need to build our own middleware

To help the server parse bodies, encode URLs, and so on.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A route immediately sends a response using JSON from req.body. Which setup prepares that data?

Register express.json() before the route.Register express.json() after the route.Register express.urlencoded() before the route.

Register express.json() before the route.

lessons.title: Question: router.route()
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which route does the instance of router.route have?

/main/users/main/app/users

Make sure to pick /main/users.
lessons.hardModeContent:
If you replace /main with /api in app.use, which request receives User created?

POST /api/usersGET /api/usersPOST /main/usersPOST /users

Make sure to pick POST /api/users.

lessons.title: Question: Import express.Router()
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's the first step to use Express Router?

We declare a variable and assign it to the Router packageWe add the app.listen() method to create the server

We declare a variable and assign it to the Router package.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Express is already imported as express. Which line creates a router instance before you add routes to it?

const router = express.Router();app.listen(3000);const router = app.get();

const router = express.Router();.

lessons.title: Question: router.use()
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is a prerequisite to run the middleware functions mounted in the path by router.use?

The requested path base must match the pathThe middleware functions must keep an orderThere is no prerequisite

The requested path base must match the path.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You mount a router with app.use(router). It uses router.use("/admin", authMiddleware).

Which request path can run authMiddleware?

/admin/users, because its base matches /admin/users, because every router middleware runsOnly /admin, because nested paths never match

/admin/users, because its base matches /admin.

lessons.title: Question: App Level
lessons.interactiveContent:
What method do we use to bind middleware at the app level?

app.userouter.usereq.use

Make sure to pick app.use.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Your app responds at /health and mounts a router at /users. A logger must run before both handlers.

Where should you register logger?

With app.use(logger) before both routes.With router.use(logger) only inside the users router.With app.use(logger) after both responding routes.

With app.use(logger) before both routes.

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
In what order are multiple middleware functions executed?

They are executed in the order they are defined, from left to rightWe can't guarantee an order in which middleware is executed

They are executed in the order they are defined, from left to right.

A route registers auth, log, then sendBooks. Each function calls next(). In what order do they run?

auth, log, sendBookssendBooks, log, authIn an unpredictable order for each request

lessons.title: Question: Error Message
lessons.interactiveContent:
When data requested by the client doesn't exist on the server, what might we add to the response in addition to the 404 status?

A message to the user that the data doesn't existA message to the user to try the request again later

A message to the user that the data doesn't exist.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A request includes a valid user ID. The database lookup succeeds but finds no user. Which response explains the result?

404 with User not found400 with Missing id parameter500 with Unexpected server error

Make sure to pick 404 with User not found.

Make sure to pick res.redirect("/new-route").

A handler must send the client from an old URL to /new-route with Express's default 302 status. Which call does that?

lessons.title: Question: next()
lessons.interactiveContent:
Why is next invoked at the end of the middleware function?

It's used to continue executing middleware functions after the first middleware executesIt's not needed here

It's used to continue executing middleware functions after the first middleware executes.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A GET request reaches /books. If next() is removed from the first middleware, what happens after Request logged is printed?

The request stops there, so the books handler is not reachedThe books handler still prints List of books sentExpress sends Request logged as the response body

The request stops there, so the books handler is not reached.
